events.title: Bay City Rollers
events.blurb:
Journey back to the carefree days of the 70s with Scotland’s well loved original boy band Bay City Rollers reigniting the global ‘Rollermania’ phenomenon that captured the hearts of fans of all ages.
With over 300 million albums sold worldwide, Bay City Rollers were among the most iconic bands of their generation, winning fans over with classic hits like ‘Bye Bye Baby’ and ‘I Only Want to Be With You’, while cementing their place in pop history.
Now, Bay City Rollers legend Stuart “Woody” Wood has assembled a powerhouse line-up of musicians who channel the spirit, sound and style of the band the world fell in love with. Backed by outstanding musical pedigrees, their passion for the music is undeniable and completely contagious.
The reborn Bay City Rollers feature Ian Thomson on lead vocals and guitar, Marcus Cordock on bass, Steve Morrison on drums, and Woody on guitar.
Their anthem ‘Don’t Let The Music Die’ still rings true with the band led by Woody, the Bay City Rollers bring fresh energy and renewed excitement to the stage, breathing new life into the classic hits for a whole new generation of fans.
The Bay City Rollers are back … and ready to turn Fringe by the Sea tartan.
Support for the night will be from Carl Marah, an Edinburgh‑based singer‑songwriter originally from Dunbar, who brings a blend of classic storytelling and modern, cinematic flair. Known for his work with psychedelic pop outfit Logan’s Close and now carving out a distinct solo identity, Marah delivers songs marked by lyrical honesty, melodic richness and an instinctive emotional pull.

Backed by a golden‑age soundtrack featuring hits like Twistin’ the Night Away, Blue Moon and Just a Gigolo, this feel‑good show blends human pyramids, backflips, fire routines and rope work with irresistible humour and charm.
Triumphantly received at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe and seen by over 650,000 spectators worldwide, the Black Blues Brothers have performed in major theatres and festivals across more than 20 countries and even for King Charles. A joyous, high‑energy celebration of music, movement and pure showmanship.

events.title: Hannah Lavery & Michael Pedersen
events.blurb:
Join award‑winning poet and playwright Hannah Lavery and Edinburgh Makar Michael Pedersen for a rich conversation about friendship, connection and the communities that shape us.
Hannah Lavery, former Edinburgh Makar and Associate Artist with the National Theatre of Scotland, is known for her incisive, socially engaged work across poetry and theatre. Her acclaimed collections Blood Salt Spring and Unwritten Woman have established her as a vital voice exploring identity, care and belonging, with a new collection, Everything, Everyday, forthcoming in 2026.
Michael Pedersen is a prize‑winning poet, author and current Edinburgh Makar. His poetry collection The Cat Prince won Best Poetry at the Books Are My Bag Readers Awards, while his memoir Boy Friends was a Sunday Times Critics’ Choice. His debut novel Muckle Flugga has been praised as “garishly alive” and “extraordinary”.
Together, they reflect on creativity, relationships and the ties that hold us in life, in art and in community.
This event is presented in partnership with Coastal Community Connections, a local charity dedicated to turning loneliness and isolation into connection.

Winner of the 2024 Yoto Carnegie Medal for Writing and recipient of an OBE, Joseph is celebrated for books such as If All the World Were…, the Luna Loves… series, Overheard in a Tower Block, and The Girl Who Became a Tree. His trademark blend of snappy dialogue, poetry and vivid storytelling makes Relic an unforgettable ride.

events.title: LOVE OF LIFE Launch
events.blurb:
Musician Erland Cooper has composed a very special piece of music for LOVE OF LIFE, rooted in the joy of slowing down and taking time to notice what’s around us.
This is the official launch of this new piece of work and of the multi-layered project as a whole at Fringe by the Sea.
Sula bassana, composed by Erland Cooper and recorded by the BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra, and the accompanying film by Lewis Gourlay will be presented for the first time.
Host Vic Galloway will be joined by Erland Cooper, Naomi Mcintosh and Lewis Gourlay to discuss their new work for the project.
Orkney-born Erland is an Emmy-nominated composer, producer and multi-instrumentalist who as a solo artist, has released five critically acclaimed studio albums, including a trilogy of work inspired by his childhood home, as well as themes of nature, people, place and time. His work often combines field recordings with traditional orchestration and contemporary electronic elements.
Feel more, feel good and feel your way forwards with some of Scotland’s most innovative creatives, through LOVE OF LIFE. Original takes on ‘biophilia’ – our innate desire to connect to nature – are open for exploration at this year’s festival. We invite you to delve in, and deepen your connection for our shared future.
Supported by The Scottish Government’s Expanded Festivals Fund through Creative Scotland.

events.title: The Flock
events.blurb:
Come and join The Flock! To celebrate the launch of LOVE OF LIFE at Fringe by the Sea, we’re inviting you to be part of a special community parade on the 31st July. A flock of handmade gannets will weave from the Harbourside in North Berwick through the town to the festival site in the Lodge Grounds, led by a stunning giant bird puppet. This is a chance to make your own puppet to carry in the parade, under the expert guidance of puppeteers Vision Mechanics, who brought the incredible 10-metre STORM to us in 2021.
We’d love your help in making this a truly eye-catching spectacle, highlighting the incredible nature all around us and the plight of seabirds. The Northern Gannets who make Bass Rock their home are, like many seabirds, facing significant threats.

You can come along to any of the sessions which will run 10am-1pm & 2pm-4pm on each of the dates. You will receive further information by email after you sign up/secure a ticket.

Recomposing Earth takes you into the mind of an artist and the magic of the Orkney Islands that inspire him, with a story that reminds us of music’s importance as an expression of the human condition.

events.title: Ben Fogle: In Conversation
events.blurb:
Ben Fogle first arrived in our world on the BBC’s groundbreaking millennium project Castaway, spending a year on the remote island of Taransay.
Since then, he has become one of Britain’s best-known adventurers and storytellers, leading teams of would be explorers through Extreme Dreams and Extreme Andes and presenting programmes including Countryfile and Animal Park as well as documentaries filmed in Botswana and Antartica.
Ben’s own expeditions are legendary, he has rowed the Atlantic with James Cracknell, setting a British record despite hurricanes, capsizes and exhaustion. The pair also raced to the South Pole, rode a rickshaw from Edinburgh to London and trekked across the empty Quarter desert.
A bestselling author, many times over, Ben continues to inspire with stories of resilience, exploration and the natural world.
He joins us for an in-depth chat about a life lived on the edge of adventure.

events.title: Maggie O’Farrell: Land

North Berwick‑raised Maggie O’Farrell returns to town where she went to high school, for a special conversation about *Land*, her 10th and most ambitious novel to date. This sweeping, multi‑generational epic opens on a windswept peninsula in the west of Ireland and follows a mapmaker, Tomás, and his young son as they chart a country devastated by the Great Hunger. When they discover an unrecorded scrap of ancient woodland, a strange encounter sends them on an odyssey that will reshape their lives and echo through generations.
Inspired by Maggie’s own family history, including her great‑great‑grandfather who worked on the Ordnance Survey, Land explores how personal stories intertwine with myth, memory, rebellion, colonisation and the landscapes that hold them. It is a spellbinding novel of separation, longing, recovery and survival in the shadow of tragedy.
Land’s publication follows the release of a film adaptation of Hamnet, Maggie’s much loved and highly acclaimed novel. Maggie will also reflect on the extraordinary success of the Hamnet film adaptation, co‑written with Academy Award‑winner Chloé Zhao and starring Paul Mescal and Jessie Buckley, which has earned a remarkable sweep of BAFTA, Academy Award®, Golden Globe and Critics Choice nominations. Maggie O’Farrell is one of the great novelists, drawing readers into fictional worlds few ever forget.

events.blurb:
After years of busking and sharing covers on YouTube, the time has come for Rianne Downey to step into the spotlight with the release of her debut album, A Consequence of Love. events.title: Lind & Lime Cocktail Masterclass

The Grand Voyage is an evolution of our botanicals; a way of expanding our world while staying true to what defines us. With every release, we explore a new citrus, shaped by its landscape and captured in our signature balance.

events.title: Belle and Sebastian
events.blurb:
Belle and Sebastian will celebrate 30 years of ‘If You’re Feeling Sinister’ by performing the iconic album in full at Fringe by the Sea, followed by a second set of classic tunes.
First released in 1996, the record has long-since attained mythic status – “greatest of all time” list fixtures with songs that have spent decades populating mixtapes and playlists. The Guardian praised ‘If You’re Feeling Sinister’ as “subtly poetic, wickedly funny, and gorgeously melodic.”
One of Scotland’s most beloved indie-pop bands, Belle and Sebastian pair thoughtful, relatable lyrics with warm melodic arrangements. Led by Stuart Murdoch, their unmistakable sound and timeless song-writing have earned them a worldwide audience and long standing place at the heart of Scotland’s music scene.
Forming in Glasgow in 1994, Belle and Sebastian have become one of the country’s most enduring and influential indie-pop bands. Over the course of 12 studio albums, the have received wide-spread critical claim and a loyal global following. Their accolades include ‘Outstanding Contribution to Music’ at the NME Awards in 2014 and Best Newcomer at The Brits in 1999, recognising their lasting impact on modern music.
Belle and Sebastian’s music has reached even wider audiences through numerous TV and film features. Their much loved track ‘The Boy With The Arab Strap’ became instantly recognisable after soundtracking the end credits of the TV hit series ‘Teachers’, while other catalogue favourites have appeared across international cinema and television including 2007’s hot film, Juno.
Support comes from Fright Years who craft emotive, cinematic indie rock that feels both. intimate and immense.

Greig Laidlaw is truly one of the biggest characters in Scottish sport. Fred MacAulay welcomes Greig for this featured conversation about his inspirational rugby career and much-lauded leadership style – with plenty of laughs thrown in for good measure!
A proud Scotsman with a fierce work ethic, Greig knew early on where he wanted to be — on a rugby pitch. Even while completing an apprenticeship as a joiner, he kept pushing, training, and closing the gap between a childhood dream and a professional career. From his Scotland debut in 2010 to his international retirement in 2019, Greig became one of the most influential figures in modern Scottish rugby. He captained his country 39 times — more than half of his 76 caps — and more than any other Scottish male player in history.
A strategist, a metronomic goalkicker, a captain with a calm edge, he was the heartbeat of Scotland through two World Cups and a British & Irish Lions tour in 2017. His club career has taken him across Scotland, England, France and Japan, winning silverware and earning the respect of every environment he entered. Wherever he has played, he has proven to be a leader you can trust, a thinker you can follow, and a competitor who raises the standards of those around him.

events.title: Unforeseen: Improvising Life and Music
events.blurb:
Unforeseen: Improvising Life and Music is a 60‑minute multimedia performance by cellist and sound artist Justyna Jablonska, exploring migration, memory and the unpredictable act of improvising a life. Blending live cello, electronics, spoken word and film, she creates a richly layered world of sound and image.
Drawing on early childhood memories, field recordings and testimonies from Polish, Ukrainian and Roma migrants, the piece weaves maternal voices, lullabies, birdsong, Eastern European folk melodies and atmospheric electronica. Its semi‑improvised form brings immediacy, intimacy and emotional charge.
Featuring a film by Anna Leszczynska, with haunting photography and animated visions of post‑industrial landscapes. Co‑directed with Fiona McKinnon and co‑written with Alex Edmonds. Supported by Creative Scotland and Chamber Music Scotland.

events.title: Kool & the Gang
events.blurb:
Kool & the Gang, officially launched in 1969. Thanks to iconic songs like Celebration, Cherish, Jungle Boogie, Summer Madness, and Open Sesame, they’ve earned two Grammy Awards, seven American Music Awards, 25 Top Ten R&B hits, 9 Top Ten Pop hits and 31 gold and platinum albums.
From Nairobi to Newark, Kool & the Gang has performed continuously longer than any R&B group in history and their bulletproof funk and jazzy arrangements have also made them the most sampled R&B band of all time. A reviewer recently called their performance “a 24-karat show” and every year, even after a half-century on the road, yields a non-stop schedule of shows across the globe.
The heavily-in-demand band has continued to tour the world, appearing most recently alongside Kid Rock, Dave Matthews Band, Elton John, The Roots, and a 50-city tour with the legendary rock band, Van Halen.
The group enjoys global fame and recognition and a following that spans generations due in part to the groups widely sampled catalogue. Kool & the Gang’s drum beats, bass, guitar and signature horn lines lace the tracks of numerous artists including the Beastie Boys, Jay-Z, Madonna, Janet Jackson, Cypress Hill, and P. Diddy. Kool & the Gang is the most sampled band in hip-hop by far. Their music is also featured on the soundtracks for Rocky, Saturday Night Fever, Pulp Fiction, Wreck-It Ralph and countless others.
Kool & the Gang’s years of hard work and talent earned them an induction into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in June 2018.

Exploding out of Edinburgh at the dying end of the twentieth century, Bombskare is Scotland’s premier ska juggernaut, renowned for their high-octane performances, crackerjack timing and impeccable dress sense. One of the tightest live bands in the UK, Bombskare has been delivering infectious, energy-packed ska for a quarter of a century. Blending classic Jamaican ska beats with punk, rock, and a twisted dose of dark humour, they’ve been a staple on the UK festival circuit for decades, captivating audiences with their upbeat melodies, devastating rhythms and hardcore hornography.
Bombskare’s debut album, A Fistful of Dynamite (2009), universally agreed as the greatest debut since ‘Straight Outta Compton’(!), saw the transition from live chaos to studio magic, while The Day the Earth Stood Stupid (2013), drew on their love of pop culture and B-movie nostalgia to showcase the band’s versatility as songwriters, without yielding an inch in energy.
In 2016, Bombskare’s talent was recognised nationally when they won the BBC’s “UK’s Best Part-Time Band” competition, cementing their status as ska legends. With their third album, A Million Ways to Die (2019), the band continues to evolve while staying true to their roots, serving up a blend of danceable grooves, punchy lyrics, and punchable brass.
2025 sees the release of Bombskare’s fourth studio outing, an 18-track tour de force, recorded during a live hiatus, and sees the band take a darker turn, both musically and lyrically, while remaining recognisably Bombskare.It showcases an increasingly diverse range of influences; from Jamaican dance halls to TV show themes, from AC-DC to XTC, you can detect it all. No genre is off limits, no cow is too sacred. All ska, zero filler, every cut a dance floor filler.
Whether headlining a festival stage or playing to packed club venues, Bombskare never fails to deliver a powerhouse performance that is guaranteed to leave a mark. Year on year, they remain at the forefront of the UK ska scene, earning them a dedicated following and making them a must-see live act.

Steeped in tradition, their music draws on decades spent at the heart of the genre. Both artists have played alongside and befriended some of the greats, from Howlin’ Wolf and John Lee Hooker to Sonny Boy Williamson. Paul Jones, renowned singer, harmonica virtuoso and long‑time BBC Radio 2 R&B presenter, brings unmatched insight into the Blues. Dave Kelly, one of Europe’s leading bluesmen, adds his signature guitar mastery and soulful vocals, honed through collaborations with icons such as James Burton and Buddy Guy.
Together, they deliver a warm, intimate performance rich with original songs, classic influences and stories from a lifetime in music.
For true Blues fans, this is everything you could hope for, and more.

Kate presents From Our Own Correspondent on Radio 4. She became a household name as BBC Chief News Reporter, covering the Gulf War, the demise of the Soviet Union, the protests in Beijing’s Tiananmen Square and NATO’s campaign in Kosovo.

Maribou State bring their stunning, immersive live show to Fringe by the Sea for one of the stand-out nights of the summer. Blending soulful electronica, deep grooves, soaring vocals and expansive beats.
Chris Davids and Liam Ivory have spent over a decade crafting a warm, organic style that blends laidback electronica with touches of soul, UK club music and rich atmospheric sounds.
Since emerging in 2011, Maribou State have become one of the most exciting names on the global dance scene. From their breakthrough album Portraits to the acclaimed Kingdoms in Colour, and their recent album Hallucinating Love, their music balances evocative samples with emotional depth, creating tracks that feel equally at home on the dancefloor or on a festival field.
Known for their immersive live performances, the duo have played everywhere from Glastonbury to the Sydney Opera House, selling out tours across the UK, Europe and North America. Their live shows combine live instrumentation, soaring vocals and deep, groove-led electronics to create an unforgettable atmosphere.
Expect smooth grooves, expansive beats and a feel-good energy as we welcome Maribou State to Fringe by the Sea.
Support act, Edinburgh duo Sarah/Shaun open the night with a surge of atmosphere, melody and electronic edge. Fresh from completing their acclaimed Visit Through The Heavy Static EP triptych, their five‑piece live setup has become one of Scotland’s most talked‑about new forces, all big hooks, big feeling and serious momentum.

events.title: Wavelength – Pauline Black: A 2 Tone Story
events.blurb:
Pauline Black: A 2-Tone Story is a documentary feature film that chronicles the trailblazing life, music career, and activism of The Selecter’s lead singer, Pauline Black.
Directed by Jane Mingay and based on Black’s autobiography, the film explores her experiences with adoption, race, gender, and her defining role in the UK ska movement.
The screening will be followed by a discussion with Pauline in conversation with host Vic Galloway.
Performer, singer, artist, band leader and songwriter, Pauline Black has dedicated four decades to the music scene and is an undisputed icon of British music. Supporting and campaigning for racial equality throughout her work, she describes herself as first and foremost, a singer. Pauline is one of very few women in the 2-Tone scene – she is often referred to as the Queen of Ska. Pauline celebrated her 70th birthday in 2023 and is still performing live with The Selecter – recently releasing new studio album Human Algebra and touring worldwide. Pauline was awarded an OBE in the in the 2022 New Year Honours and received an Honorary Degree from the University of Warwick in the same year.
A lifelong love of music inspired by punk and reggae artists from the 1970s led Pauline to join The Selecter and a career that has seen her travel across the world to share her passion and artistry with hundreds of thousands of fans. The Selecter went on to become a platinum-selling band and one of the most influential within the 2-Tone music scene and are known the world over for hits including “Three Minute Hero,” “Missing Words,” “Too Much Pressure” and “On My Radio”. 2025 marks the 45th anniversary of their debut album Too Much Pressure.

events.title: Ian Hislop: In Conversation
events.blurb:
Renowned comedian, author and broadcaster Ian Hislop is the iconic Editor of magazine ‘Private Eye’ and captain of long-standing TV series ‘Have I Got News For You’.
We’re delighted to welcome Ian to Fringe by the Sea for an intimate conversation exploring the stories and insights from his remarkable career spanning more than 40 years.
After studying English Literature at Oxford University, Ian was appointed editor of the satirical ‘Private Eye’ in 1986, guiding it to both critical acclaim and commercial success. With his signature wit and satirical approach, Ian offers sharp social and political commentary through investigative journalism. Published fortnightly, Private Eye maintains a loyal readership of over 700,000 and is known for its annual edition, authored by Ian in recent years.
Beyond journalism, Ian has showcased his talents as a playwright, writing acclaimed works such as A Bunch of Amateurs, Trial by Laughter and The Wiper Times. Ian has also produced many celebrated documentaries for BBC Television and BBC Radio 4 across history, literature, and comedy.
Ian will be available for a (time-limited) book signing after the event. His book will be available to purchase at the event during Fringe by the Sea (31st July-9 August) through Night Owl Books.

With over 1.7 million followers on Instagram, LEVI.SCT has sparked a global movement. His performances explode with virtuosity, rhythm and raw emotion, pulling new generations into the world of classical music and leaving audiences on their feet. In 2025, he was crowned Contemporary Pianist of the Year at the Pianote Awards, a defining moment in a meteoric rise.
His debut world tour launched in 2026 with sold-out shows in Paris at La Cigale and London’s Union Chapel. He has also performed at renowned halls including Elbphilharmonie and Flagey, captivating audiences worldwide.
Now, he brings this explosive, genre-defying spectacle to close Fringe by the Sea in unforgettable style, a finale set to shake the coast and leave you buzzing as the final note fades.
